title: Natural tracer concentrations do not fix recharge or storage scale in a fully mixed store with unknown liquid loss
abstract: We test whether natural stream-water tracers can resolve a flow-only ambiguity in proposed explanations for persistent runoff loss. For one fully mixed store with unknown recharge volume and non-stream liquid loss, an exact scale transformation preserves flow and all concentration records, including tracers with known first-order decay. For a linear store driven by known rain, we derive sharp bounds on recharge and stream coefficients. In 81 synthetic models, recharge ranged from 17.5% to 100% of rainfall while flow and three tracer records agreed within 6e-15. A head record with unknown storage coefficient also left the scale unresolved. A known store volume or a known tracer mass delivered to that store removed the scale ambiguity. Nine nonlinear checks and an independent reduced-equation audit passed. This is a theory and measurement-design result. It does not identify the regional cause, test field mixing or prove that whole transitions between eras are indistinguishable. Code, synthetic inputs, bounds tool, proofs, results and provenance are included.

display.caption: Synthetic models have the same flow and natural concentrations across a wide recharge range. Absolute volume or a known store tracer mass removes the scale ambiguity.
